text: function brings Positional Accuracy Improvement (PAI) framework raster geospatial data (e.g., scanned historical maps, aerial imagery, digital elevation models, thematic raster grids). Forward vs. Inverse Mapping Raster Warping: vector PAI shifts existing vertices forward (\((x, y) \(x + dx, y + dy)\)), raster data exists rigid, regular grid. Applying forward mapping raster pixels result irregular point cloud gaps ("holes") expanded areas collisions compressed areas. produce valid, regular raster grid, apply_pai_raster employs inverse (backward) mapping: Defines regular coordinate grid target (corrected) raster. Projects target cell center backwards transformation find corresponding location source (distorted) image. Resamples pixel value source raster using requested interpolation method. Model Inversion Handling: Models trained direction = "inverse": Directly evaluate displacement target source coordinates single step. Helmert models (direction = "forward"): Uses exact closed-form analytical inverse 4-parameter similarity transformation. Non-linear models (gam, tps, rf, svmRadial, lm): Employs rapid iterative fixed-point backward mapping algorithm converges sub-millimeter precision within 2 iterations. Interpolation Methods: "bilinear" (Default): Bilinear interpolation. Recommended continuous rasters elevation models, satellite/aerial imagery, scanned paper maps. "near" "simple": Nearest-neighbor assignment. Essential discrete, integer, categorical rasters (e.g., land cover classification, soil classes, parcel IDs) ensure original class values preserved without generating non-existent intermediate values. Performance Optimization (mesh_step): Evaluating non-linear models (like GAM Random Forest) individually across millions raster cells can computationally demanding. setting mesh_step (e.g., 10 20), apply_pai_raster computes exact displacements regular subsampled grid mesh uses high-performance C++ bilinear interpolation (terra::resample) reconstruct continuous displacement field across full raster grid. provides orders--magnitude speedups maintaining sub-pixel accuracy.
